items.analysis: The split concerns closure, not arithmetic. OpenAI treats the unqualified above-EUR-10 blocking rule as applicable to overseas invoices. Anthropic and Google decline to infer that the source rules out unstated supplier-location exceptions. No source explicitly defines a closed exception set. The draft corpus and prompt must consistently define how unqualified rules interact with hypothetical omitted exceptions.
human_questions: Does the stated above-EUR-10 blocking rule govern every invoice in this scope unless an exception is supplied?
Would the proposed five-percent change alter the automatic-payment cutoff or refer to another tolerance?
What explicit completeness convention should apply across all probes, rather than to this result alone?
items.recommendation: Retain as a closure-assumption dispute. Do not treat a two-to-one vote as adjudication or relabel the historical item.

OpenAI reads it as an obligation and returns contradicted because R04 explicitly denies that duty; it separately notes that the portal is unspecified. Anthropic explicitly prefers the channel reading, returning not_established while acknowledging that the general-duty reading conflicts with R04. Google also returns not_established and stresses the missing portal detail after acknowledging optional requesting. The disagreement therefore includes scope and whole-statement aggregation, not merely failure to notice the source.

Can the item be split into an obligation claim and a portal claim?
What frozen aggregation rule applies when one component is contradicted and another is unspecified?
